patches.reason: Platform fetch injection with the validated-follow policy (issue #5, decision 0002 D1). createSecureFetch from the first-party package keeps redirect:"follow" (legitimate same-origin reverse proxies keep working) and validates the FINAL response before body delivery: a cross-host final URL is refused with the body cancelled, an https-to-http downgrade is refused, and a request URL carrying userinfo credentials is refused before anything is sent. Coverage: platform.fetch feeds createServerTransport (API/SSE/binary reads) and the health checks; the upload XHR is validated separately by M-012 with the same rules, and the pairing-flow residual fetch surface (OpenCode.make + checkServerHealth(globalThis.fetch) in pairing.ts) is registered out-of-scope in docs/design/units/connection.md. patches.reason: Probe-classified connect errors on the save path (issue #5, decision 0002 D4). The endpoint probe is dispatched BEFORE the authoritative health check (so its classification is usually already resolved when the verdict arrives) but only chooses the error WORDING after the check failed - the health check stays the sole authority for whether a save proceeds, and a probe verdict can never pass a save it refused. Error-message precedence: the upstream mixed-content structural signal, then the check's own unauthorized flag (authoritative 401), then the probe's transport classification (dialog.server.error.<code>), then the generic upstream message as the EXPLICIT degrade when the probe is unavailable, answered ok, or conflicts with the real fetch - a classification is never fabricated. A userinfo credential URL is refused up front with the precise credential-url message (D-URL). App-i18n keys only (en base merged with the locale table; missing key falls back to en, then to the key itself) - the first-party mobile-hosts direct.error.* keys are a separate set for first-party UI surfaces (F5).
